title: Developmental error-correction makes mutations neutral and builds up cryptic variation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Developmental error-correction makes mutations neutral and builds up cryptic variation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: By buffering mutational effects through developmental regulation, the multiscale competency architecture makes neutral many mutations that would be deleterious under a direct genotype-to-phenotype mapping, so they persist as a pool of phenotypically dormant cryptic variation that can later be exploited.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: MCA makes many mutations neutral that would be deleterious in a direct genotype → phenotype architecture. Such mutations whose effects are mitigated by developmental regulation are not weeded out; instead, they persist, generating over time a rich pool of diversity that may be phenotypically dormant, but can be exploited in future.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Implications of multiscale competency for the evolutionary process”. Scope: Evolving populations of organisms with regulative development

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cryptic genetic variation and buffering are measurable and supported by public variation and perturbation resources. Existing datasets test subsets and proxies but rarely identify the proposed developmental architecture and evolutionary fate together.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify mutations buffered to normal phenotype under intact development, reveal their effects after disrupting regulation, and test whether such variants segregate at higher frequencies than equivalent unbuffered deleterious variants. Later environmental or regulatory shifts should expose usable phenotypic variation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Future exploitability is difficult to infer from current frequency.

Dormant effects require matched genetic and developmental perturbations.

Neutrality can result from redundancy unrelated to multiscale competency.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.42
data existence: 0.65

operationalizability: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cryptic genetic variation can be surveyed in Drosophila resources, and the competency model can show mutations hidden from selection by a developmental layer. Those are partial proxies. They do not identify multiscale competency, as opposed to other buffering, as the cause of a dormant pool that evolution later exploits.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the fraction of mutations that are phenotypically silent under normal development and revealed under a perturbation, in a system with regulative development, and compare with a direct genotype-to-phenotype encoding if one is available. A larger silent pool that later becomes visible would support cryptic variation produced by buffering; absence of that pool, or a pool explained by protein chaperones rather than developmental correction, would count against the competency-specific version.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cryptic variation is well documented for chaperones and redundancy, which are rivals to multiscale competency.

FlyBase does not record a pool of mutations buffered specifically by anatomical error correction.
